Draws and expectations of both counts from the joint model

Source: R/predict.R
posterior_predict_y1_and_y2.Rd

posterior_predict_y1_and_y2() draws the pair (y1, y2) from the joint model of the fit, with new shared and source-exclusive components on every draw. posterior_epred_y1_and_y2() returns the marginal means of the two counts, mu + lambdaone and mu + lambdatwo. Neither function conditions on a recorded count. The y1 slice of posterior_predict_y1_and_y2() has the distribution of the draws of posterior_predict(), and the y1 slice of posterior_epred_y1_and_y2() equals posterior_epred(). Both functions return an array in the shape that brms uses for a multivariate model: posterior draws by observations by response.

The two counts are drawn together: the y1 and y2 of each draw share one draw of the shared component N_s, so the covariance of the drawn counts is Var(N_s), as in the model. The package has no separate function for y2, because draws of y2 made apart from the draws of y1 would not share a draw of N_s with them. Marginal draws of y2 are draws[, , "y2"], where draws is the result of posterior_predict_y1_and_y2().

Usage

posterior_predict_y1_and_y2(
  object,
  newdata = NULL,
  re_formula = NULL,
  ndraws = NULL,
  draw_ids = NULL,
  ...
)

posterior_epred_y1_and_y2(
  object,
  newdata = NULL,
  re_formula = NULL,
  ndraws = NULL,
  draw_ids = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

object

A brmsfit from bipois(), bipois_partialobs(), binegbin(), or binegbin_partialobs().

newdata

An optional data frame; if NULL, the data of the fit are used. See Details.

re_formula

A formula for the group-level effects to include, passed to brms::prepare_predictions(). NULL (the default) includes all group-level effects, and NA includes none.

ndraws, draw_ids

Passed to brms::prepare_predictions() to select posterior draws.

...

Further arguments to brms::prepare_predictions(), such as allow_new_levels.

Value

A numeric array with dimensions posterior draws x observations x 2, with the third dimension named y1 and y2. The values from posterior_predict_y1_and_y2() are integers.

Details

For each posterior draw of the parameters, the three components N_s, N1, and N2 are drawn independently from their distributions, and posterior_predict_y1_and_y2() returns y1 = N_s + N1 and y2 = N_s + N2. The marginal moments are

$$E[y_1] = \mu + \lambda_1, \qquad E[y_2] = \mu + \lambda_2, \qquad \mathrm{Cov}(y_1, y_2) = \mathrm{Var}(N_s),$$

with \(\mathrm{Var}(N_s) = \mu\) for bipois and \(\mathrm{Var}(N_s) = \mu + \mu^2 / \phi_s\) for binegbin, where \(\phi_s\) is shapes. The variance of each count is the sum of the variances of its two components, for example \(\mathrm{Var}(y_1) = \mu + \mu^2/\phi_s + \lambda_1 + \lambda_1^2/\phi_{x1}\) for binegbin.

A predictive check of the pair, such as of the variance of the difference y1 - y2, needs draws of both counts from posterior_predict_y1_and_y2(). Subtracting the recorded y2 from draws of posterior_predict() treats the two counts as independent and overstates that variance by \(2\,\mathrm{Var}(N_s)\).

New data. The recorded y1, the recorded y2, and the observation indicator do not affect the result. The column y1 may be omitted from newdata, but brms requires every variable named in the vint() term, so newdata must contain y2 and, for a fit from a _partialobs() constructor, the observation indicator. The values in these columns are not used, so any integers will do, such as 0 or -1. The same is true for newdata in posterior_predict() and posterior_epred().

See also

posterior_predict_y1_given_y2() for draws of y1 conditional on the recorded y2; vignette("prediction") for a summary of the prediction functions.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
library(brms)

# 500 units. y2 is recorded on every unit, and y1 on about 20% of units.
set.seed(20261115)
dat <- rbicount(
  500,
  mu        = 4,
  lambdaone = 1,
  lambdatwo = 2,
  shapes    = 2,
  shapexone = 4,
  shapextwo = 4
)
dat$y1_obs  <- rbinom(nrow(dat), 1, 0.2)
dat$y1_true <- dat$y1
dat$y1[dat$y1_obs == 0] <- -1L

fit <- brm(
  bf_mfd(
    y1 | vint(y2, y1_obs),
    logM      ~ 1,
    logitf    ~ 1,
    delta     ~ 1,
    kappas    ~ 1,
    kappaxone ~ 1,
    kappaxtwo ~ 1
  ),
  family   = binegbin_partialobs(),
  stanvars = binegbin_partialobs_stanvars(),
  data     = dat,
  prior    = c(
    prior(normal(1.5, 1), class = "b", nlpar = "logM"),
    prior(normal(0, 1.5), class = "b", nlpar = "logitf"),
    prior(normal(0, 0.5), class = "b", nlpar = "delta"),
    prior(normal(0, 1),   class = "b", nlpar = "kappas",    lb = 0),
    prior(normal(0, 1),   class = "b", nlpar = "kappaxone", lb = 0),
    prior(normal(0, 1),   class = "b", nlpar = "kappaxtwo", lb = 0)
  )
)

# Predictive check of the variance of the difference, on the paired rows
paired <- dat[dat$y1_obs == 1, ]
yrep <- posterior_predict_y1_and_y2(fit, newdata = paired, ndraws = 500)
var_d_rep <- apply(yrep[, , "y1"] - yrep[, , "y2"], 1, var)
hist(var_d_rep)
abline(v = var(paired$y1 - paired$y2))

# Expected counts of the two sources on each paired unit
ep <- posterior_epred_y1_and_y2(fit, newdata = paired)
dim(ep)
} # }
